jobs.title: Digital Operations Graduate
jobs.description:
Starting Salary
: £32,000 plus an annual bonus and benefits

Location
: Goole

Duration
: 24 months

Closing date:
31st December 2026- Please note, we may close this advert earlier than advertised if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible

Imagine contributing to projects that help move millions of people every day?

At Siemens Mobility, we're developing innovative transport solutions that are transforming the future of rail and making travel more sustainable. Start your career at the heart of that journey!

Are you an ambitious final year undergraduate looking for a unique graduate programme?

Join a two-year graduate journey that combines hands-on experience with structured development. Through technical and professional training, graduate workshops, mentoring and leadership exposure, you'll build your skills while working on meaningful projects. You'll collaborate with fellow graduates across the business, present your achievements and deliver a Business Impact Project with real business value, developing the confidence, experience and connections needed to accelerate your career at Siemens Mobility.

Our Rolling Stock and Customer Service keeps trains running safely and reliably every day. The business delivers expert maintenance, technical support and digital solutions across the full lifecycle of rail fleets, helping customers maximise performance, availability and passenger satisfaction.

Year 1: Complete a tailored programme of rotations across operational, technical, depot, and business functions, combined with time in your substantive role, to gain hands-on experience and develop a broad understanding of Rolling Stock Customer Services.

Year 2: Transition into your substantive team to develop deeper expertise and prepare for your role beyond the graduate programme.

You‘ll Make a Difference By

Ready to start your career at the heart of a major UK rail operation?

Working alongside engineering, maintenance and operational teams to develop digital solutions that solve real challenges across our rail fleets.
Supporting the development of data-driven tools and technologies, helping turn operational requirements and fleet data into practical solutions that improve maintenance, reliability and decision-making.
Getting involved across the full digital product lifecycle, from identifying use cases and capturing requirements through proof of concept, testing, validation and deployment into the operational environment.
Exploring technologies such as data analytics, dashboards, automation and AI, and understanding how they can be applied safely and effectively within a complex railway environment.
Working directly with depot teams and end users, gathering feedback, understanding operational challenges and ensuring the tools we create deliver genuine value.
Building a combination of technical, commercial and stakeholder-management skills, giving you the experience needed to become a future leader in digitalisation and rail engineering.

What You’ll Need To Succeed

We are seeking innovative and inquisitive candidates that demonstrate the following:

Achieved or be on track to achieve a 2:2 or above in:

Mechanical Engineering
Electrical / Electronic Engineering
Digital Engineering/Transformation
Railway / Rail Systems Engineering
Engineering Management
Industrial Engineering
Logical thinking, willing to self-learn and research, and take a creative approach to problem solving
Ability to work independently, safely and responsibly; take ownership of challenges and ideas and are looking to develop your ability to drive and lead change
Enjoy collaborating with others to find innovative solutions.

Transform The Everyday with us

We value your unique identity and perspective and are fully committed to providing equitable opportunities and building a workplace that reflects the diversity of society. Come bring your authentic self and transform the everyday with us!

We are a Disability Confident Leader and welcome applications from all individuals, including those with disabilities. If you require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please contact your recruiter, who will be happy to support you.

jobs.title: Data Engineer Apprenticeship - Level 4
jobs.description:
Office for National Statistics

Location Newport and Titchfield (Fareham)

Job grade Executive Officer

Contract type Fixed term

Working pattern Flexible working, Full-time, Part-time, Compressed hours

Salary £29,545

Closing date Wed 18 Nov 2026

Reference 487695

Profession Digital, Data & Technology

Apply now

If you are interested in an exciting career in data and technology and want to become a highly skilled tech professional, we are seeking 5 people who are passionate about data and technology to join our Data Engineering teams on an apprenticeship programme.

The roles will be working in Data Products, Services and Governance (DPSG), which sits centrally within ONS, provides a cross-ONS capability for data, including data access and preparation, and the provision of data and linked data products.DPSG develops and manages the systems and processes that underpin the distribution of data across ONS and beyond. DPSG provides data to ONS, academia, wider government, and other external users in a safe and controlled way, supporting and encouraging users to maximise data utility, enabling innovation and statistical and research use.

As a Data Engineer Apprentice, you will study towards a Level 4 Data Analyst apprenticeship and combine your job and hands-on experience with virtual learning and will include one to-one with tutors and mentors, tutorials, and research projects.

You will work with appropriate technologies as a Data Engineer apprentice, you’ll gain the technical expertise to take your career in an exciting new direction. By the end of the apprenticeship, you will have achieved an industry-standard qualification and have the skills to progress your career in line with your aspirations.

Responsibilities

Identify, collect, and migrate data to/from a range of internal and external systems.
Use a range of analytical techniques such as data mining, time series forecasting and modelling techniques to identify and predict trends and patterns in data.
Assist with data quality checking and cleansing and how to resolve issues.
Assist production of data visualisation including performance dashboards and reports.
Summarise and present the results of data analysis to a range of stakeholders
Application of coding standards. Write clear and well documented code in Python using industry and organisational best practices
Business Analysis/ User requirements validation;
Matching and linking of datasets using statistical matching techniques;
Become familiar with Cloud developments and technology

Part-time candidates will be considered, subject to a minimum of 30 hours per week
, apprenticeship provider requirements and business needs.

What qualification will I get?

The programme will be 2 years and will be delivered by assigned external training providers. The apprenticeship will support apprentices to develop their capability in data engineering. As well as training and support from the external training providers you will have support from a dedicated, highly experienced data engineering mentor.

All apprentices who successfully meet the scheme's milestones will receive a Level 4 Data Analyst Diploma.

You will gain experience to help you work towards your qualification, as well as attending formal training and other development opportunities that will consist of 20% off-the-job learning.

You will develop other skills that will aid you in the workplace, such as organisation, communication, the ability to work under pressure, teamwork, and lots more, giving you a real and valuable insight into the industry.

Person specification

Essential Criteria

Can manage own workload, and work effectively as part of a team, to ensure deadlines or outputs are met.
Can analyse information or evidence from a variety of sources to draw conclusions and inform decision making.
Can communicate complex or technical ideas, both in writing and verbally, to stakeholder with differing levels of knowledge or experience.
Identifies opportunities to make improvements and gets the support of relevant people to implement the changes.
Takes opportunities to develop own skills and share knowledge with colleagues.
A passion for technology and a keen technical interest.

Standard Eligibility Criteria For Apprenticeships Apply

You must reside and work in England or Wales.
You must have been at least 16 years old by 31st August 2026.
You must not already have an equivalent qualification of the same type, content, and level (or higher). (Example computer science degree)
You must not be in fulltime education or undertaking another apprenticeship at the same time.
You should hold a GCSE in Maths and English at Grade C or above, an equivalent qualification, or relevant experience in lieu of a qualification may be considered.

The training provider makes the final decision on whether funding can be provided per person and the job offer will be made on the condition that funding is available.

Apply now

jobs.title: Threat Intellience Analyst
jobs.description:
Department:
Global Security Services
Location:
UK - London

Description

We’re looking for a Threat Intelligence Analyst who can turn complex cyber incident data, telemetry and external threat information into intelligence that people can genuinely use.

Sitting within our Cyber Exposure & Risk Intelligence team, you’ll identify meaningful patterns in cyber activity, assess threat actor behaviour and emerging trends, and translate your findings into clear insights for clients, brokers, underwriting teams and wider business stakeholders.

Your analysis will have a practical impact. It will contribute to client reports, broker content, workshops and recurring intelligence products, as well as proactive notifications and alerts. You’ll also have the opportunity to develop confidence presenting your findings to clients and external audiences.

Key Responsibilities

Analyse cyber incident data, telemetry and external threat sources to uncover trends, patterns and emerging risks.
Turn complex data into clear, relevant intelligence for reports, alerts, presentations and workshops.
Produce high-quality written intelligence for clients, brokers and internal stakeholders.
Lead cyber insight sessions, client workshops and threat-modelling exercises.
Contribute to recurring threat reporting and build repeatable analytical outputs.
Assess threat actors, campaigns, tactics, techniques and procedures, connecting technical activity to real-world risk exposure.
Help shape the team’s analytical questions, hypotheses and priorities.
Contribute to external reports, presentations and thought-leadership content

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

You’ll be an analytical and curious thinker who enjoys getting beneath complex datasets and turning what you find into a clear story. Crucially, you’ll be able to connect technical observations to real-world risk and business impact, communicating your findings effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.

You’ll bring: Experience in cyber threat intelligence, incident analysis, cybersecurity consulting or a related analytical role.
A good understanding of the cyber threat landscape, including threat actors and attacker methodologies.
Strong analytical skills and the ability to extract meaningful insight from complex information.
Strong written communication skills, with the ability to create clear and well-structured outputs for different audiences.
Confidence presenting findings and contributing to workshops, structured analysis or intelligence-led discussions.
Strong critical thinking and intellectual curiosity, with the confidence to develop and articulate your own views.
A collaborative, outcome-focused approach centred on producing useful, actionable intelligence.

Experience analysing trends or working with operational or incident datasets would be advantageous.

You’ll have a STEM degree or equivalent analytical experience, while relevant cyber certifications such as GCTI, GCIA, CTIA or CISSP are beneficial rather than essential.

Core Values

Love what you do:

We show up each day ready to take on the world. Our passion and intensity set us apart and makes the difference to our colleagues, customers, brokers and carriers.

Challenge everything:

We’re never afraid to question the way that things are done and we constantly challenge ourselves and others to makes things better.

Have fun, be good:

Insurance is a serious business, but we don’t take ourselves too seriously. We make it fun to work at CFC, we welcome all viewpoints, and we treat everyone how we would expect to be treated.

Show less

Not Applicable

Full-time
